topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: swap call-sites to op-core/* across op-node, op-service, op-batcher
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. See plan §1, §2, §3, §4, §5 in the op-geth decoupling doc (PR #19767).

## Goal

Once the `op-core/*` packages exist, swap all relevant call-sites in the Go services so they stop reaching into op-geth internals. No behaviour change — just imports and types.

## Scope

### DepositTx construction / decoding

Replace the `types.NewTx(&types.DepositTx{...}).MarshalBinary()` pattern throughout op-node with `optypes.DepositTx{...}.MarshalBinary()` — the `*types.Transaction` wrapper is eliminated, we go straight from struct to `[]byte`. Files to edit:
- `op-node/rollup/derive/deposits.go`, `deposit_log.go`, `parse_upgrade_transactions.go`
- `op-node/rollup/derive/*_upgrade_transactions.go` (Ecotone, Fjord, Holocene, Isthmus, Jovian, Interop, Karst)
- `op-node/rollup/interop/indexing/attributes.go`

`UnmarshalDepositLogEvent` returns `*optypes.DepositTx`.

### Transaction methods → helpers

- `tx.IsDepositTx()` → `optypes.IsDepositTx(tx)`
- `tx.SourceHash()` / `tx.Mint()` / `tx.IsSystemTx()` → decode raw bytes via `optypes.UnmarshalDepositTx` and read fields, or use helpers from #20262.
- `tx.From()` on a deposit tx (single call site in `op-node/rollup/interop/indexing/attributes.go:105`) → same pattern.
- `tx.RollupCostData()` → `opfees.TxRollupCostData(tx)`.

### Receipt (`*optypes.Receipt`) in `op-service/txinclude`

- `op-service/txinclude/interfaces.go` `EL.TransactionReceipt` return type → `*optypes.Receipt`.
- `op-service/txinclude/persistent.go`, `monitor.go`, `txbudget.go`: update references.
- Replace inline operator-fee math in `txbudget.go` and `isthmus_cost_oracle.go` with `opfees.OperatorCost(gasUsed, scalar, constant)`.
- Replace `types.NewL1CostFuncFjord` with `opfees.NewL1CostFuncFjord`.

### `OptimismConfig` and `ChainConfig`

- `rollup.Config.ChainOpConfig *params.OptimismConfig` → `*opparams.OptimismConfig`.
- `rollup.Config` gets any missing hardfork timestamp fields (KarstTime, InteropTime if not already present).
- `op-service/eth/BlockAsPayload` and `BlockAsPayloadEnv`: replace `config *params.ChainConfig` parameter with a local `HardforkConfig` interface (`IsCanyon(uint64) bool`, `IsIsthmus(uint64) bool`). Callers pass `rollup.Config` directly.

### EIP-1559 helpers

- `op-node/rollup/derive/payload_util.go`, `rollup/interop/indexing/attributes.go`, `rollup/attributes/engine_consolidate.go`: switch imports from `github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/consensus/misc/eip1559` to `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-core/eip1559`.

### Superchain loader

- `op-service/superutil/` is deleted (the function moved to `op-core/superchain` in #20259).
- `op-node/rollup/superchain.go`, `op-node/chaincfg/chains.go`: switch imports from `github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/superchain` to `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-core/superchain`.

## Dependencies

Blocked on: #20260 (`op-core/params`), #20261 (`op-core/fees`), #20262 (`op-core/types`), #20259 (`op-core/superchain` + `op-core/eip1559`).

topIssues.title: kona|acceptance-tests: TestSequencerPreset does not support kona sequencer
topIssues.author: pcw109550
topIssues.body:
Found while attempting to run monorepo acceptance tests targeting kona-node.

After init test:
https://github.com/op-rs/kona/blob/47b2f1c6ee1b340d65161c3a13160c8d070fec21/tests/node/reorgs/init_test.go

```go
	l2Config := node_utils.ParseL2NodeConfigFromEnv()

	fmt.Printf("Running e2e reorg tests with Config: %d\n", l2Config)

	presets.DoMain(m, node_utils.WithMixedWithTestSequencer(l2Config))
```

Even if 
```go
		KonaSequencerNodesWithGeth: 1,
		KonaSequencerNodesWithReth: 1,
```
are enabled, preset `WithMixedWithTestSequencer` does not use these field

https://github.com/op-rs/kona/blob/47b2f1c6ee1b340d65161c3a13160c8d070fec21/tests/node/utils/test_sequencer_preset.go

leading that the kona sequencer not spawning even if the preset is configured.

Also need to take a look at this logic:
```go
func WithMixedWithTestSequencer(l2Config L2NodeConfig) stack.CommonOption {
	if l2Config.OpSequencerNodesWithGeth == 0 && l2Config.OpSequencerNodesWithReth == 0 {
		l2Config.OpSequencerNodesWithGeth = 1
	}
```
So the preset is intentionally not using op-node sequencer, it overrides to use the op-node as a sequencer.

This causes `simple-kona-sequencer` network not spawning kona sequencer. For example, you can run 
```
just test-e2e-sysgo-run node node/reorgs "simple-kona-sequencer" TestL2ReorgAfterL1Reorg
```
and check sequencer logs. The logs detail show op-node sequencer is spawned, which was not intended.

topIssues.title: kona-node: implement syncmode.offset-el-safe for behavior parity with op-node
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
Track adding `syncmode.offset-el-safe` to **kona-node** for behavior parity with op-node.

## Background

op-node #21033 (merged 2026-05-27) changed the default of `--syncmode.offset-el-safe` from `0` to `12h` (the OP Mainnet sequencing window). The feature: after **execution-layer (EL) sync** completes, instead of trusting the synced tip as safe/finalized, op-node retracts the safe and finalized heads to `tip - ceil(offset / blockTime)` blocks. This forces derivation to re-derive the most recent ~12h of blocks before they are considered safe. The option is only effective when `--syncmode=execution-layer`.

kona-node currently has **no equivalent**. After EL sync, `L2ForkchoiceState::current()` simply reads the EL's `Safe`/`Finalized` tags (falling back to genesis), with no offset.

## op-node references (behavior to match)

- `OffsetBlockNum` / `DurationToBlocks` — `op-node/rollup/sync/start.go:119` (`n = ceil(offset/blockTime)`, `target = head - n`, clamped to genesis)
- `headsAfterELSync` — `op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go:874` (unsafe stays at tip; safe & finalized retract to `tip - n`)
- flag + ineffective-unless-EL-sync warning — `op-node/service.go:350-366`, `op-node/flags/flags.go:134`

## Where it slots into kona

- Apply the offset in the EL-sync-complete reset path: `mark_el_sync_complete_and_notify_derivation_actor` (`rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/engine/actor.rs:159`) → `reset()` → `find_starting_forkchoice`.
- The tip is resolved in `L2ForkchoiceState::current()` (`rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/sync/forkchoice.rs:46`); apply the retraction right after.
- Add the config field + CLI flag in `rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/`.

## Work items

1. Add `offset_el_safe: Duration` (default `12h`) to the node sync config + a `--syncmode.offset-el-safe` CLI flag, including op-node's "ineffective unless EL sync → warn and ignore configured value" handling.
2. Port `OffsetBlockNum` / `DurationToBlocks` (ceil division, genesis clamp) as a small Rust helper.
3. In the EL-sync-complete reset path, when `offset > 0`: keep `un_safe = tip`, set `safe = finalized = block(tip.number - n)`.

## Open design decision

op-node layers two robustness behaviors that **cannot be ported faithfully** because kona-node has **no safedb and no persisted safe head**:

- **safedb resume** — N/A in kona; kona would always use the raw offset head (acceptable; safedb is only an optimization).
- **never-retract** — op-node never moves safe/finalized below the engine's current heads on restart, so the offset window is only re-derived once. Without a persisted safe head, a naive kona port would re-derive the offset window on **every restart after an EL sync**.

  Mitigation: kona already gates the post-EL-sync reset on `finalized_head == default` (genesis), so the offset can be applied **only on the initial post-EL-sync reset** to avoid repeated re-derivation. This should be confirmed during implementation.

## Acceptance

- kona-node retracts safe/finalized by `ceil(offset/blockTime)` blocks (default 12h) after EL sync completes, only when running EL sync.
- No repeated re-derivation of the offset window on subsequent restarts.

_Filed as parity follow-up to op-node #21033._

topIssues.title: Fix super-root migration runbooks for simplified SUPER_PERMISSIONED
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
The single-chain and shared-factory super-root migration runbooks still assume the old fault-game behavior for `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` game type 5. They configure op-challenger with the unsupported `super-permissioned` game type and prescribe a nonzero initialization bond even though the simplified game is bondless and OPCMv2 requires its bond to be zero.

Update both runbooks to use a zero type-5 bond, configure op-challenger for type 9 only where it is enabled, and document that type 5 relies on op-dispute-mon, guardian blacklisting, and the separate anchor-advancement workflow.

topIssues.title: [PCD] Commit genesis timestamp at anchor selection
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body: The L2 genesis block header carries a timestamp that propagates into the genesis block hash, the `rollup.json` consumed by the fault proof program at compile time, and the genesis output root. All three artifacts must agree on a single value, and that value must be fixed before the off-chain pipeline starts running. At the anchor-selection stage, compute `genesis_time = anchor.timestamp + X` and persist it to deployer state. `X` is an operator-configurable offset sized to cover the runtime of the off-chain pipeline plus the L1 inclusion latency of the deploy transaction, so that `genesis_time` is still in the future when `OPCM.deploy()` is mined. Every downstream stage reads `genesis_time` from state and never recomputes it, which is what makes reruns idempotent.

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth): runtime cross-unsafe head (eth_crossUnsafeHead)
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in, repeatable `--rollup.cross-unsafe-head-source-rpc CHAIN_ID=RPC_URL` flag to op-reth that exposes `eth_crossUnsafeHead`. The endpoint reports the latest local block, seeded from the local safe head, whose executing (cross-chain) messages have been runtime-validated against the configured source-chain RPCs.

Supersedes #20650 (rebased onto latest `develop`, with review fixes and an end-to-end acceptance test added).

## How it works

- When source RPC mappings are configured, op-reth builds a `CrossUnsafeHeadExt` merged into the `eth` namespace and (if the `eth` module is enabled) spawns a lightweight 5s background poller to keep an in-memory validation cache warm.
- On each call/tick it re-anchors to the local safe head, drops any cached block that is no longer canonical locally or whose source dependencies are no longer canonical on their source chain, then walks forward toward local latest validating new blocks.
- For each executing message it fetches the claimed source block + logs from the source RPC, checks the origin, recomputes and compares the payload hash, and checks the initiating timestamp. Missing/erroring source RPCs and any mismatch **fail closed** for the candidate block.

## Scope / limitations (intentionally a simplified runtime gate)

- Does **not** implement the full supervisor dependency graph (no cycle/hazard analysis, dependency-set activation, or cross-chain frontier semantics).
- Expiry uses the default `MESSAGE_EXPIRY_WINDOW`; it does not track a dependency set's `override_message_expiry_window` (noted in code).
- The cache mutex is held across a refresh's source RPCs (bounded by a per-request timeout); concurrent callers serialize during a refresh.

## Tests

`op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/crossunsafe` — two-chain interop, op-reth on the destination chain with the flag pointing at the source chain:

- `TestCrossUnsafeHeadAdvancesPastValidatedExecutingMessage` — proves the head validates and advances past a real executing message **while that block is still unsafe** (above the safe head), so it can only be reached via runtime validation against the source chain.
- `TestCrossUnsafeHeadStopsAtInvalidExecutingMessage` — includes a genuinely-invalid executing message kept unsafe-only and proves the head advances up to the prior block but **never crosses** the invalid one.

> Note: this is a draft; CI / a final local acceptance run on the rebased base is being confirmed and the PR will be updated if anything needs fixing.

topPRs.title: docs: add hardfork registry and regroup notices into release-train framing
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#970

## What

One permanent registry page per OP Stack hardfork (Regolith → Lagoon) with structured frontmatter — lifecycle, superchain-default activation timestamps, governing spec link, governance approval, minimum component versions — plus `scripts/generate-hardforks.ts`, which validates the schema, cross-checks every activation against the superchain-registry configs, and renders the generated activation tables under `snippets/generated/hardforks/` (`pnpm gen:hardforks` / `gen:hardforks:check`). A frontmatter edit is the only way to change an activation row.

`op-stack/protocol/network-upgrades.mdx` becomes the registry index: its hand-maintained table (already stale — the Karst row still said "pending / TBD" after the 2026-07-08 mainnet activation) is replaced by the generated summary. The Notices tab is regrouped into Network Upgrades / Deprecations / Operations with **no URL moves and no new redirects**; the notices overview now frames notices as transient action items and the registry as the permanent record.

Shared artifact: this is the single hardfork-registry implementation shared by the Option B (slice B4) and Option A (slice 6) docs programs — A6 consumes these pages, the schema check, and the generated tables.

## Why

Upgrade facts were scattered across Notices, per-page banners, and a hand-edited table that had already drifted. Facts that change often now live in structured data validated against source (superchain-registry); prose lives in pages.

## Source citations

*   Activation timestamps: `superchain-registry` `superchain/configs/{mainnet,sepolia}/superchain.toml`; Regolith's genesis activation: `rust/alloy-op-hardforks/src/optimism/{mainnet,sepolia}.rs`; Bedrock anchor: registry `mainnet/op.toml [genesis]` (block `105235063`, timestamp `1686068903` — corrects the old page's `1686079703`, which contradicted its own block arithmetic).
*   Spec links: `ethereum-optimism/specs` `specs/protocol/<fork>/overview.md` (all 11 verified; deep anchors resolved against spec headings); rendered-site links per the cross-repo link policy.
*   Minimum versions: the Upgrade 19 / 17 / 15 and Holocene notices in this repo, cited on each page.

## Verification

An independent adversarial accuracy pass re-derived every claim before this PR opened: all 18 activation rows re-checked against a fresh read of superchain-registry `main` @ `738212ef2932d26f9274e3317699471534d2b3ac` (the same commit the monorepo submodule pins); block estimates recomputed from the genesis anchors; spec overviews and deep anchors re-fetched from `ethereum-optimism/specs@main`; min-version tables re-checked against the in-repo notices; `gen:hardforks:check` confirmed to fail on a deliberately corrupted timestamp and on a registry fork with no page, and the committed snippets confirmed byte-identical to a fresh regeneration.

## Nav / serialization note

This PR touches `docs.json` (Protocol Information group + Notices regroup). Per the docs.json serialized lane it rebases on demand as other nav PRs merge; its two hunks do not overlap the docs.json regions touched by the currently open docs-improver nav PRs. Nav validator, redirect lint, and link-policy linter are green with zero baseline/allowlist growth; `mint broken-links` reports only the 5 findings already present on `develop`.

## Reviewer checklist

*   [ ] Spot-check two activation rows against the superchain-registry
*   [ ] `pnpm gen:hardforks:check` passes (requires the superchain-registry submodule or `--registry`)
*   [ ] Notices regroup reads correctly (no URL moves intended)
*   [ ] Follow-up (not this PR): the Upgrade 19 notice still describes Karst as "proposed / pending governance approval" post-activation — it should be refreshed/archived

See `projects/docs-improver/README.md` for program context.

topPRs.title: fix(op-challenger): advance anchors for super permissioned games
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds lifecycle-only handling for `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` games so finalized games can advance their `AnchorStateRegistry` without making game type 5 playable.

Separates lifecycle support from trace playability, registers lifecycle bindings independently of configured players, routes supported games through post-game handling, and simulates `setAnchorState(game)` against the game-selected registry before submission. Adds an acceptance scenario using the real type-5 proposer and op-challenger, verifying that the ASR advances to a type-5 anchor after the finality delay.

Closes ethereum-optimism/optimism#21708

Tested with the focused SuperPermissioned acceptance scenario, affected Go package suites, and `just lint-go`.
